summary: The note surveys policies for sustainable urban development, using examples from many cities and experts. It covers green city plans, data-driven governance, green jobs, green infrastructure, participatory governance, resilience, transportation, renewable energy, housing and success metrics. It argues that integrating green infrastructure, economic growth and adaptable frameworks will lead cities toward a resilient, equitable future.
one_line: Overview of city policies for sustainable urban development, from green plans, data platforms and renewables to transport, housing, participation and metrics.
key_facts: According to the World Bank, cities occupy just 3% of the Earth's land but account for 70% of global carbon emissions and over 60% of resource use.
The UN projects a 68% urban population by 2050.
On September 10, 2023, Mayor Jane Smith of Greenfield City unveiled 'The Green City Plan', featuring expanded public transport, renewable energy installations and a 'green belt'.
C40 Cities data suggests investing in public transit, building efficiency and waste management could cut greenhouse gas emissions by 90% by 2050, delivering up to $24 trillion in economic benefits.
Metropolis Monitor, launched August 15, 2024 by the city of Techville under Mayor Andrew Brown, uses IoT sensors to monitor traffic flow, energy consumption, air quality and water usage.
The UNEP Green Jobs Report states that investment in sustainable energy could create 24 million new jobs worldwide by 2030.
Mayor Thomas Keller of Riverside City said on November 1, 2023 that green infrastructure includes green roofs, permeable pavements, water reclamation systems and urban agriculture.
Coastal City's 'Community First' initiative uses town halls and open forums to gather citizen input; Linda Hernandez highlighted participatory governance on December 12, 2023.
Harbor City's Coastal Barrier Expansion project, despite initial opposition, helped mitigate flood damage during an unexpected superstorm.
A February 20, 2024 report by the Sustainable Transport Action Network found cities with comprehensive cycling, walking and transit networks cut transportation-related emissions by up to 25%.
Mayor Kim Lee of SolarCity announced on March 8, 2024 that the city produces 50% of its energy from solar sources.
On April 30, 2024, the Urban Development Department introduced the Affordable Green Housing program, offering incentives for energy-efficient, affordable housing.
Habitat III took place in Quito in October 2016.
